critical_steps: Lower K-frame bounds are exactly the scalars A with A K K* <= S.
Positive definiteness of S converts this to a norm condition on S^{-1/2}K.
The published bound uses two separate spectral inequalities and is optimal only when both can be saturated by the same vector.
The explicit Parseval example has true optimal bound 1 while the published quotient is 1/4.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact operator-order reduction, exact two-dimensional Parseval K-frame counterexample, and equality conditions for two spectral inequalities.
integrity.unproved_limits: No singular-frame-operator pseudoinverse formula is asserted, and no novelty claim is made for general Douglas-factorization descriptions of optimal K-frame bounds.

scientific_limitations: The exact inverse-square norm formula is stated under the positive-definiteness assumption on the frame operator used in the disputed proposition.

A 2020 paper is reported by later primary literature to contain general optimal K-frame bounds; its full theorem text was not accessible during the bounded source inspection, so novelty is claimed for the source-specific counterexample and equality criterion rather than for abstract optimal-bound theory.
An unindexed correction or inaccessible source may contain the same counterexample or equality criterion.
title: The smallest frame-operator eigenvalue need not be the optimal lower K-frame bound
